plan.title: UC inflamed vs control: GSVA hallmark pathway scores + heatmap
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question asks for a per-sample pathway activity score and a heatmap showing which pathways separate treated (UC inflamed) from control colon samples — this is a per-sample scoring question (GSVA), not a group-level ranked GSEA question, though the DE step is retained because GSVA works best on variance-stabilized expression and because a DE contrast gives the group labels needed to test which of the 50 Hallmark scores differ significantly. The pipeline: (1) QC the 12-sample design (6 UC-inflamed vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch), explicitly inspecting sample_01's low library size (~4x below median) rather than silently dropping it; (2) filter and normalize counts with DESeq2's standard median-of-ratios approach, obtaining a blind VST matrix as the expression input for GSVA; (3) run GSVA with the Gaussian kernel on the VST matrix against the MSigDB Hallmark human gene set collection (50 sets) to produce one activity score per pathway per sample; (4) test each of the 50 Hallmark scores between UC-inflamed and control with limma (moderated t-test, same design as the count-level model) to identify which pathways significantly separate the groups; (5) render the full sample x pathway score matrix as a heatmap annotated by condition, ordered/highlighted by the limma significance, so the pathways driving group separation are visually apparent; (6) report the scores table, the limma results, and diagnostics (including how sample_01 behaved) with full reproducibility metadata.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) + PCA + sample distance heatmap
Keep genes with >=10 counts in >= smallest group size
DESeq2 design ~condition, explicit reference level = control
GSVA per-sample pathway activity scores on log-normalized/VST counts with Hallmark gene sets, then limma moderated t-test on scores vs condition, heatmap of scores
Summary report with pathway score heatmap and limma results table
